name: Context Engineering Pipeline
description: One YAML builds a governed, searchable, citeable knowledge base out of raw unstructured text: chunk -> classify -> embed -> write_vector_store. Pairs with rag_pipeline (query side). Receipt-ready: every chunk is stamped with the provenance a retrieval gateway needs to record context receipts (see `resources/context_receipt_store`). Free/local by default (sentence-transformers + HuggingFace zero-shot + ChromaDB); litellm for any provider; execution_mode='sql' runs the whole chain server-side in Snowflake Cortex / BigQuery / Databricks so the corpus never leaves the warehouse.

inputs.description: Raw text rows, either from an upstream asset (upstream_asset_key) or a direct SQL query (source).

outputs.description: Final step's output rows -- chunked, classified, and/or embedded, depending on the steps configured.

upstream_asset_key.label: Upstream Asset Key
upstream_asset_key.description: Upstream asset key providing a DataFrame of raw text rows. Mutually exclusive with `source` -- set exactly one.

source.label: Source
source.description: Pull raw text rows directly via SQL instead of from an upstream asset: {kind: warehouse_query, resource_key: <registered resource>, sql: <query>}. Works out of the box with duckdb_resource and any resource exposing .get_engine() or .get_connection(). Mutually exclusive with `upstream_asset_key` -- set exactly one. On a partitioned asset `sql` may use {partition_key}, {partition_start}, {partition_end} (time-window partitions) and {partition_key.<dim>} (multi-axis); each is replaced by a complete escaped SQL string literal, so write `WHERE d = {partition_key}` without quotes. `{{` / `}}` are literal braces.

id_column.label: ID Column
id_column.description: Column uniquely identifying each source row -- threaded through to every chunk as a citation back to the source.

text_column.label: Text Column
text_column.description: Column containing the raw text to chunk.

metadata_columns.label: Metadata Columns
metadata_columns.description: Additional source columns to carry forward onto every chunk row -- available to later steps and written as vector-store metadata for filtered search.

max_source_rows.label: Max Source Rows
max_source_rows.description: Safety cap on source rows processed per materialize (python mode only). A real corpus is typically too large for one in-memory run -- pair with partitioning to bound each run to a slice instead of the whole historical corpus.

execution_mode.label: Execution Mode
execution_mode.description: 'python' (default): pulls rows into a DataFrame, works with every provider. 'sql': the whole chunk/classify/embed chain runs as one query in the warehouse's own engine via a native AI function -- data never leaves the database, no in-memory size limit, but only for warehouses with a native embedding/completion function (set sql_dialect).

sql_dialect.label: SQL Dialect
sql_dialect.description: Required when execution_mode='sql'. Selects which warehouse-native AI SQL functions to emit.

output_table.label: Output Table
output_table.description: Required when execution_mode='sql'. Fully-qualified destination table the resulting knowledge base is written to, in the same database.

incremental.label: Incremental (SQL mode)
incremental.description: execution_mode='sql' only. Reuse the embeddings and categories already in the output table instead of paying the warehouse AI function for the whole corpus every run. A prior embedding is reused when the chunk's content_hash matches and the stored embedding_model equals the current model; a prior category when content_hash matches and the stored category_signature (hash of candidate_labels) equals the current one. Only chunks without a reusable value reach the AI function. The first run, or a table lacking the needed columns, builds in full. Set false to recompute everything every run.

steps.label: Steps
steps.description: Ordered list of {id, op, ...op-specific fields} dicts. Each step's `source:` names a prior step's id to read from; if omitted, defaults to the immediately preceding step. Valid ops: 'chunk' (must be first), 'filter', 'dedupe', 'sensitivity', 'stamp', 'enrich', 'classify', 'embed', 'write_vector_store'. filter/dedupe/sensitivity/stamp/enrich are python-mode only.

retrieval_eval.label: Retrieval Eval
retrieval_eval.description: A golden set that gates this knowledge base: {queries: [{query, expected: [chunk or source ids]}], k: 5, min_recall: 0.8, min_mrr: null, severity: ERROR|WARN, blocking: false}. After the index is written, each query is embedded with the same embed step and run against it; the `retrieval_quality` asset check reports recall@k and MRR and fails below the thresholds, with `blocking: true` holding downstream assets until it passes. Pair with code_version: a new recipe must still answer the golden questions. Python mode needs a chromadb index; execution_mode='sql' (bigquery, snowflake_cortex, databricks) runs it warehouse-side by cosine similarity over the whole output table.

context_policy.label: Context Policy
context_policy.description: Declare the governance policy a retrieval gateway should enforce for this knowledge base: {scope: <chunk metadata field naming the tenant>, sensitivity: public|internal|confidential|restricted, max_age_hours, token_budget, retention_days, access_tags: [...]}. Recorded on the asset as `context/policy` metadata and `context/*` tags; read back with context_policies() in resources/context_receipt_store. Same declaration as the @context_asset decorator.

code_version.label: Code Version
code_version.description: Dagster code_version for the asset: the identity of the recipe that builds this context. Defaults to a fingerprint of the steps (chunking, filters, embedding model...), so changing the recipe marks the asset stale in Dagster (AutomationCondition.code_version_changed) and every chunk is stamped with it (`source_code_version`), letting outcomes be compared across recipe versions. Set it explicitly to tie it to something else, such as a git SHA of this config.

emit_data_version.label: Emit Data Version
emit_data_version.description: Emit a content-derived Dagster data version (hash of every chunk id + content hash + the build recipe). Dagster's default data version derives from the asset's code version and its inputs' data versions, so it changes on every run when an upstream asset has no explicit version (a typical raw table); without this a no-op rebuild would make anything that recorded the old version (such as context receipts) look stale.

stamp_provenance.label: Stamp Provenance
stamp_provenance.description: Write source_asset_key, source_version (the emitted data version), source_partition, source_id, chunk_id, content_hash and embedding_model onto every chunk in the vector store, so a retrieval gateway can build receipts directly from index hits. Python mode: the write_vector_store step. SQL mode: columns chunk_id, content_hash, source_asset_key, source_version (content hash of the whole table), source_partition, source_code_version on the output table.

description.label: Description
description.description: Asset description shown in the Dagster catalog.

deps.label: Deps
deps.description: Lineage-only upstream asset keys (no data passed at runtime).

owners.label: Owners
owners.description: Asset owners -- list of team names or email addresses.

asset_tags.label: Asset Tags
asset_tags.description: Additional key-value tags to apply to the asset.

kinds.label: Kinds
kinds.description: Asset kinds for the Dagster catalog. Auto-inferred if unset.

include_preview_metadata.label: Include Preview Metadata
include_preview_metadata.description: Include a preview of the output data in metadata.

preview_rows.label: Preview Rows
preview_rows.description: Rows to include in the preview metadata when include_preview_metadata is True.

retry_policy_max_retries.label: Retry Policy Max Retries
retry_policy_max_retries.description: Max retries on asset failure. Defines a RetryPolicy.

freshness_max_lag_minutes.label: Freshness Max Lag Minutes
freshness_max_lag_minutes.description: Maximum acceptable lag in minutes before the asset is considered stale.

freshness_cron.label: Freshness Cron
freshness_cron.description: Cron schedule string for the freshness policy.

partition_start.label: Partition Start
partition_start.description: Partition start date (ISO), required for time-based types.

partition_dimensions.label: Partition Dimensions
partition_dimensions.description: Multi-axis partition spec: list of {name, type, start, values, dynamic_partition_name} dicts (type: daily/weekly/monthly/hourly/static/dynamic). One entry is a single axis; several make a MultiPartitionsDefinition. Mutually exclusive with the flat partition_* fields. In execution_mode='sql', `source.sql` can use {partition_key.<name>} for each axis.

backfill_policy.label: Backfill Policy
backfill_policy.description: Backfill execution strategy for a partitioned asset. 'multi_run' launches one run per partition (optionally capped via Backfill Max Partitions Per Run); 'single_run' materializes a whole backfill range in one run. Leave empty for Dagster's default (one run per partition). Ignored when the asset is not partitioned. In execution_mode='sql', single_run is only allowed when `source.sql` uses both {partition_start} and {partition_end} (the query must itself select the whole range) and the asset is not multi-dimension; otherwise the build raises.

backfill_policy_max_partitions_per_run.label: Backfill Max Partitions Per Run
backfill_policy_max_partitions_per_run.description: For Backfill Policy = 'multi_run' only: maximum partitions materialized per run. Leave empty for Dagster's default (1).

receipts.label: Receipts
receipts.description: Learn from real use: read the retrieval receipts recorded by resources/context_receipt_store back into every build. {resource_key: <registered ContextReceiptStoreComponent>, window_days: 30, min_retrievals: 5, min_outcomes: 3, refresh_priors: true, scope_to_recipe: true, stamp: true, quarantine: {mean_outcome_below: -0.3, mode: flag\|exclude}, regression_check: {min_outcomes: 10, max_drop: 0.15, severity: WARN\|ERROR}, rewrite_below: -0.3, prune: {never_retrieved_after_receipts: 200, mode: flag\|exclude, min_age_days: <defaults to window_days>}}. Right before write_vector_store each chunk is stamped with feedback_retrievals / feedback_rated / feedback_mean_outcome / feedback_cited / feedback_prior (so a gateway can rerank), chunks users keep rating badly are flagged or (mode: exclude) left out of the index until their old receipts age out of the window, and the run reports dead weight, best/worst chunks, rewrite_candidates (chunks at or below rewrite_below with their source id), exclusion reasons and outcomes per recipe. prune handles dead weight (zero retrievals in the window): flagged with feedback_dead_weight, or (mode: exclude, chromadb / SQL mode) left out until a later build re-adds them; it only judges when the window holds at least never_retrieved_after_receipts receipts of the current recipe, and never judges chunks younger than min_age_days (feedback_first_seen_at). regression_check adds the `recipe_outcomes` asset check: is the current recipe doing worse in production than an earlier one? Feedback is scoped to the current recipe (code_version) by default so a recipe change starts fresh. Python mode reads a ContextReceiptStore resource. In execution_mode='sql' (sql_dialect bigquery / snowflake_cortex / databricks) the same feedback is computed inside the one CREATE TABLE statement by SQL joins against the receipt tables: {dataset: <where the receipt tables live, required: 'project.dataset' on BigQuery, 'DATABASE.SCHEMA' on Snowflake, 'catalog.schema' on Databricks>, table_prefix: '', resource_key: <optional; defaults to source.resource_key and must be the same warehouse resource>, plus the same window_days / min_retrievals / min_outcomes / scope_to_recipe / stamp / quarantine / regression_check}; refresh_priors and write_vector_store do not apply (feedback_prior is read from context_item_scores as written), and mode: exclude drops the rows from the output table.

dataset.label: Receipt Dataset
dataset.description: execution_mode='sql' only. Where the receipt tables live: 'project.dataset' (BigQuery), 'DATABASE.SCHEMA' (snowflake_cortex), 'catalog.schema' (databricks); a bare schema name is also accepted. They hold the receipt tables (context_receipts, context_receipt_items, context_receipt_events, context_item_scores). Required in SQL mode; not allowed in python mode.

table_prefix.label: Receipt Table Prefix
table_prefix.description: execution_mode='sql' only. Prefix on the receipt table names, e.g. 'prod_' reads prod_context_receipts. Letters, digits and underscore only.

per_step_ops.label: Per Step Ops
per_step_ops.description: When True, emit each configured step as its own @dg.op inside one op graph instead of folding the whole chain into a single @asset -- one visible, individually re-executable-on-failure asset node per step (chunk/classify/embed/write_vector_store/...), same shape as AgenticPipelineComponent's per_step_ops. The asset key for the FINAL step stays `asset_name` unchanged (so any existing upstream_asset_key pointing at this component's output keeps working); every OTHER step publishes as `<asset_name>_<step id>`, with real step-to-step lineage between them (not just every step depending on the raw upstream). Supported with execution_mode='sql' too: each participating step (chunk always, classify/embed if configured) becomes its own real warehouse table instead of one combined CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE statement, with incremental reuse preserved per table (write_vector_store has no SQL equivalent either way, so a SQL-mode pipeline tops out at 3 steps/tables). Not yet supported combined with partitioning in sql mode (per-table partition staging is a tracked follow-up), nor with freshness_max_lag_minutes in either mode (AssetsDefinition.from_graph has no per-output freshness-policy plumbing).
